threads_text: Jensen Huang asked four tiny robot ducks to sit, nap and do somersaults on stage in Berlin, and some of them fell over. Preorders for the $399 Microduck then passed 20,000. Would you buy a robot duck for Christmas?
caption:
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang put four Microduck robots through a live demo at GTC Berlin.
The video went viral, and Hugging Face says preorders for the $399 duck passed 20,000.
The open source robots are expected to ship by Christmas.

Would you buy a robot duck for Christmas?

site_article.headline: Microduck preorders pass 20,000 after Jensen Huang's GTC Berlin demo
site_article.dek: The $399 open source robot from Hugging Face's Pollen Robotics unit went viral after NVIDIA's CEO put four of them through voice commands on stage.
site_article.summary: A video of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang playing with Microduck robots during his GTC Berlin keynote spread widely, and Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue said preorders passed 20,000 the next day. The $399 robot is expected to ship in time for Christmas.
site_article.seo_title: Microduck robot preorders top 20,000 after Jensen Huang demo
site_article.seo_description: Hugging Face's $399 Microduck robot passed 20,000 preorders after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang showed it off at GTC Berlin, according to TechCrunch.
site_article.answer_summary: Microduck is a $399, roughly 10 inch open source robot duck from Pollen Robotics, part of Hugging Face. Preorders passed 20,000 after Jensen Huang demoed it at GTC Berlin, and it is expected to ship before Christmas.
site_article.hero_alt: Microduck, a small duck-shaped robot, in a promotional photo from Pollen Robotics.

paragraphs.text: Preorders for Microduck, a $399 open source robot made by Hugging Face's Pollen Robotics unit, passed 20,000 units after NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang showed the robots during his keynote at GTC Berlin, TechCrunch reported on October 23, 2026. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue shared the milestone the day after a video of the demo spread online.

During the keynote, Huang gave voice commands to four duck shaped robots, asking them to sit, stand, nap and do somersaults. According to Superpower Daily, three toppled over when told to nap, one wandered before falling, and a couple completed the somersault. One robot got back up after a fall and returned to Huang. TechCrunch described the robots making small R2-D2 style sounds as they performed.

Huang said the robots were trained in the cloud on NVIDIA systems and then refined in an Omniverse digital twin, a simulation of the robot, according to Superpower Daily. NVIDIA's RTX Spark account posted a clip from the demo on X on October 21.

Delangue said Microduck could become the best selling robot of the year and suggested the buyers include adults as well as children, TechCrunch reported. Superpower Daily noted that the 20,000 figure reflects preorders rather than deliveries, and that the first purchasing window reportedly sold out.

Hugging Face unveiled Microduck on August 27, 2026, with a $399 price before taxes and shipping and a target of shipping before Christmas, TechCrunch reported at the time. The robot stands about 25 centimeters, or roughly 10 inches, tall and weighs under two pounds. It carries 15 motors, a camera, lidar and two inertial measurement units.

The robot can waddle, crouch, get back up after a fall, pick things up with its beak and roller skate with an accessory set of wheels. Its behaviors are trained in a physics simulation and then deployed to the hardware, and owners can fine tune them, teach it new tricks and share them with other users. Hugging Face has published the software kit, the simulation and the reinforcement learning stack on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license, according to tbreak.

Microduck is Hugging Face's second robot after Reachy Mini, which sells for $499, with a $399 Lite version. TechCrunch's August report also noted that apps installed on the robot can access its camera and microphones and may send that data to outside services.

Pollen Robotics, the French company that builds Microduck, was acquired by Hugging Face in April 2025. TechCrunch reported that NVIDIA bought Hugging Face in September 2026, which places the robot inside NVIDIA's growing robotics business.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the demo worked as marketing precisely because it was imperfect. A small, cheap robot that falls over and gets back up is easier to relate to than a polished humanoid, and the preorder count suggests consumer robotics may grow first through toys and hobby kits.
The next test is delivery: whether Pollen Robotics can ship tens of thousands of units to North America and Europe by Christmas, and how many owners go on to train and share new behaviors.
